extracted.intended_audience: media scholars, journalism researchers, and news professionals interested in how audience metrics influence editorial selection
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and factors that shape editors' decisions about which stories to publish online, with emphasis on audience web metrics, news values, platform logics, and individual/organizational influences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience web metrics as gatekeeper
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience metrics influence editors' selection decisions — the study 'examines the effects of audience web metrics on editors' and presents a snapshot of the hierarchy-of-influences model in the new media environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey of 318 gatekeepers; implies that measures of audience behavior (pageviews, clicks, engagement data) function as a gatekeeping input in editorial decision-making and should be considered alongside professional and organizational norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: News values: emotions, surprise, social impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media editors 'accentuate those elements in a story that fulfil the news values of emotions, surprise, and social impact.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific story attributes are highlighted to increase engagement; editors may reframe or prioritize content that maximizes emotional reaction, unexpectedness, or perceived societal impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: User-engagement as a primary news value
rubrics_metrics.description: News values of social media editors are described as 'user-engagement ... driven' (i.e., editors prioritize content that generates user interaction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical consequence: selection and presentation decisions are often optimized for metrics that indicate engagement (shares, likes, comments), potentially at the expense of other journalistic values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithm-driven editorial logic (platform influence)
rubrics_metrics.description: News values of social media editors are 'algorithm driven' and social media editors 'marry the Facebook logic with journalistic standards.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors adapt story elements and headlines to fit platform algorithms and affordances (e.g., Facebook's surfacing mechanisms), meaning algorithmic visibility becomes a criterion in story selection and framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalist experience reduces reliance on audience metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience in journalism 'negatively correlates with the perceived usefulness of audience metrics for enacting consumer-oriented objectives' — 'the higher the amount of journalism training, the lesser journalists will be inclined to use audience metrics in their news work.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual-level professional training and norms can lead to skepticism about using metrics for editorial decisions; experience/training is a moderating factor in metric adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial position within hierarchy shapes attitudes toward metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: A news-worker's 'position within an editorial hierarchy seems to be an important individual-level factor in shaping one's role orientations and attitudes toward audience metrics.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational role (e.g., junior vs. senior editor) influences how much weight is given to audience metrics, suggesting that policy and power structures determine metric-driven practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchy-of-influences model applied to new media
rubrics_metrics.description: The study 'provides a snapshot of the hierarchy-of-influences model in the new media environment' by analyzing how audience metrics affect editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This model implies multiple levels (individual, organizational, external/platform) interact to determine editorial selection; audience metrics are one layer among professional norms, organizational constraints, and platform influences.
